heading: Friday, November 20, 2026
topLine: Anthropic closed its Nasdaq debut up 17% at $97.17 and took in $93.5B once the greenshoe was exercised, but on day two the shares fell about 12% before the open as a broad AI sell-off spread.

items.headline: Update: Anthropic jumps 17% in its Nasdaq debut, then gives back most of the gain as an AI sell-off spreads
items.summary: ANT opened at $111.50 on Thursday and closed at $97.17, against an $83 IPO price. Underwriters exercised the greenshoe option for another $12.2B, so the IPO raised $93.5B in total ($119.5B including the private placement). On Friday the stock was down about 12% before the open as AI shares sold off worldwide. At the opening bell, Dario Amodei said Anthropic will "pace the training and deployment of AI systems" until it is confident they are safe.

items.headline: Google's Gemini app for Mac can now use your computer for you
items.summary: Gemini on macOS can now work across native apps, files and the web in the background. It shows a live preview, and you can pause, stop or approve each action. The feature is available in English in the US to AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers. It puts Gemini alongside the desktop agents from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta.

image.alt: Google's header image for Gemini computer use on Mac

items.headline: Apple job listing shows it is building its own agent that uses apps, browses and codes
items.summary: Bloomberg spotted a listing for a manager to lead an "AI agent that can use a computer" across apps, browsers, command lines and APIs. Apple is also adding macOS 27.3 warnings that discourage users from giving third-party agents full control of their Macs. Bloomberg reports a launch could come as soon as late next year, and Apple did not comment.

items.headline: Unconfirmed: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
items.summary: On his website, Alpöge posted a four-page note titled "Remark" and wrote, "I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis." He also posted a Lean formalization and says the method extends to the Generalized RH. No outside expert has yet confirmed that the Lean code builds or that its final theorem actually states RH, and Anthropic has not commented. Treat this as a claim until it is checked. It was the top AI thread on Hacker News (287 points).

items.headline: Google Research's PaperOrchestra, a multi-agent system that writes research papers, climbs GitHub trending
items.summary: This framework from Google Cloud AI Research turns ideas and experiment logs into LaTeX manuscripts, with literature synthesis, plots and diagrams. The page notes it is not an official Google product. It gained 492 stars in a day and now has about 5.3k.

items.headline: Physics of Language Models 4.2: architecture differences only show up at trillion-token scale
items.summary: Zeyuan Allen-Zhu ran 64 pretraining runs at 1.3–8B parameters and 1–2T tokens. Canon layers (local token mixing) saved about 30% of pretraining tokens for the same MMLU score at 8B. Linear-attention models that match Transformers on benchmarks still cannot reliably retrieve from a 500-token context. No model beat chance on a simple two-hop task. The takeaway: small synthetic tests reveal weaknesses that standard benchmarks hide.

items.headline: Learning theorists prove the weak sample compression conjecture with an O(d² log² d) scheme
items.summary: Cai, Moran, Warmuth and coauthors show that every binary concept class of VC dimension d has a sample compression scheme of polynomial size. The best previous bound that depended only on d was exponential (Moran–Yehudayoff, 2016). The stronger O(d) conjecture, open since 1995, is still unsolved. This is a human result and has not yet been peer reviewed.

items.headline: Jeveration makes a whole image in one forward pass, about 78 ms each
items.summary: NUS researchers fit LoRA adapters and output heads to a frozen Qwen3.5-4B so it predicts all of an image's codes in parallel. A shared random state keeps those predictions coherent. One 5.2B checkpoint does text-to-image (0.74 GenEval), image-to-image and dense prediction, and the authors report it as up to 122× faster than Janus-Pro-7B. It was the top Hugging Face daily paper (125 upvotes).

image.alt: Jeveration teaser figure showing single-pass generated images

items.headline: WeightCode: a language model writes programs that edit a network's weights to add new skills
items.summary: Instead of fine-tuning, a frozen LLM writes "weight programs" that install new computations directly into a trained network. They raised exact-match accuracy on unseen command compositions from 0% to 99.8%, and added 8.8–17.6 points of ImageNet robustness without hurting clean accuracy. Rerun on independently trained ViTs, the programs kept 83–110% of those gains.

items.headline: House panel: Commerce approved about 880,000 Nvidia and AMD AI chips for Chinese firms, a third to military-listed companies
items.summary: Records released by the House Foreign Affairs Committee show BIS approved 879,868 H200 and MI325X chips across 21 licenses between December and May. Tencent was approved for 150,000, Alibaba for 75,000 and Baidu for 43,000, and the Pentagon lists these buyers as Chinese military companies. Little actually shipped because Beijing blocked large imports. Nvidia says it has stopped shipping H200s to China, and Lutnick and former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang are expected to testify before Congress.

items.headline: Ex-Qwen lead Junyang Lin's Pragmatik Labs is valued at $5B, 2.5× its August round
items.summary: Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter, that the Shanghai agent startup raised tens of millions of dollars from HyT Capital, CDH Investments and Geely. That comes three months after a $2B first round backed by Tencent.

items.headline: Unconfirmed: Nvidia is reportedly in advanced talks to buy diffusion-LLM startup Inception for $500M+
items.summary: The Information reports that Nvidia is near a deal for Inception, which builds diffusion-based language models that generate text in parallel rather than one token at a time. Neither company has confirmed it.
